Harm Reduction

How to prevent a bad trip

By HowToEdibles Editorial Team January 15, 2024 4 min read

Tips and harm reduction advice to avoid a bad experience with cannabis edibles. Learn what to do and what not to do.

Home / Articles / How to Prevent a Bad Trip

Quick answer

Start with 2.5 to 5 mg of THC and wait at least 2 hours before taking more, because edibles take 30 minutes to 2 hours to kick in. Avoid alcohol and other drugs, and stay somewhere calm and familiar. If you have taken too much, lie down somewhere quiet, breathe slowly and sip water. The feeling usually passes within a few hours. Call 911 for chest pain, trouble breathing or fainting, and call Poison Control (1-800-222-1222 in the US) if a child has eaten an edible.

Table of Contents

  • The do's and don'ts
  • Having a bad trip right now?
  • Why edibles are stronger

Cannabis edibles can be an incredible experience when approached with care. But because they take longer to kick in and hit harder than smoking, it's easy to accidentally overdo it. The good news is that a bad trip is almost always preventable. Follow these simple guidelines and you'll have a safe, enjoyable time.

The do's and don'ts

    DO!

  • Eat a small amount at a time (2.5 to 5 mg THC), and wait at least 2 hours between doses.

  • Eat real food before you try an edible.

  • Remember that eating weed edibles is much stronger than smoking it.

  • Be aware that edibles can take up to 2 hours to kick in.

  • If you get anxious, try to stay calm. A fatal overdose from cannabis alone is unlikely, and the feeling will pass.

    DON'T!

  • Don't eat pot food too quickly. Start small and low.

  • Don't get dehydrated, make sure to drink water.

  • Don't try to get as high as possible. It's not a competition.

  • Don't take edibles on an empty stomach.

  • Don't mix edibles with other drugs.

Having a bad trip right now?

If you're having a difficult experience, remember: you are safe, the feeling is temporary, and it will pass.

Try to find a comfortable, quiet place. Breathe slowly. Drink some water. Having a trusted friend nearby can help. If someone has chest pain, trouble breathing, fainting or severe vomiting, call 911.

Get help now →

Why edibles are stronger

When you eat cannabis, your liver converts THC into 11-hydroxy-THC, which crosses the blood-brain barrier more effectively and produces a more intense, longer-lasting effect than inhaled THC. This is why edibles hit harder and last longer — often 4–8 hours — compared to smoking.

The delay (30 minutes to 2 hours) before effects kick in is the most common reason people overconsume edibles. Use our dosage calculator to plan a safe dose before you start.

This page is general harm-reduction information, not medical advice.

Sources

  1. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Cannabis Frequently Asked Questions. Signs of using too much cannabis, and why edibles can take up to 2 hours.
  2. U.S. Food and Drug Administration. FDA Warns Consumers About the Accidental Ingestion by Children of Food Products Containing THC.
  3. Monte AA, Shelton SK, Mills E, et al. Acute illness associated with cannabis use, by route of exposure: an observational study. Annals of Internal Medicine. 2019;170(8):531-537. doi:10.7326/M18-2809
